From S1B, the +DC voltage is routed to the line voltage regulator, D5 limits the DC voltage applied.
If the wires are reversed, D1 and D4 are forward biased routing positive polarity power to the line voltage regulator.
Normally, the green wire is positive and the red wire is negative. D2 and D3 are forward biased routing positive polarity power to the line voltage regulator.
This prevents damaging the telset IC chips if the green and red wires are mistakenly reversed.
D1 through D4 ensures that the DC power applied to the line voltage regulator is the correct polarity.
S1A closing shorts out R1 and C1 allowing the small level voice signals and DC power to reach the circuits in the telset through closed S1B.

For simplicity, let's look at a discrete block diagram of a typical electronic telset.
